input_messages.content: Hello, I’m having some trouble with my mobile data. It either stops working or is very slow, and I really need it to be excellent. I’m not very good with technology, so I’d appreciate some help getting this fixed. I don’t have access to Wi-Fi, so I need my mobile internet to work perfectly. Can you help me with this?
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. Let me know what you need me to do next.

I checked my phone’s status bar, and I see an airplane icon (✈️ Airplane Mode) and something that looks like a lock with “VPN Connected.” I don’t see any signal bars or anything about 4G or 5G. What should I do next?

Okay, I turned off Airplane Mode. Now I see one bar for signal (it looks pretty low), it says “2G,” and there’s something that says “Data Disabled.” I still see the VPN lock icon too. What should I do next?

I turned on mobile data. Now I see “Data Enabled,” but it still says “2G” and the signal is still just one bar. There’s also something called “Data Saver” showing, and the VPN lock icon is still there. What should I do next?
I changed the network mode like you said. Now my phone shows four bars for signal, it says “5G,” and “Data Enabled.” The “Data Saver” and VPN lock icons are still there. What should I do next?

I turned off Data Saver and disconnected the VPN. Now I see four bars for signal, “5G,” and “Data Enabled.” The VPN and Data Saver icons are gone. What should I do next to check if my internet is excellent now?
I tried to check my internet speed, but it says there’s no connection. I’m not sure what happened—everything looks good on the status bar, but it still won’t work. What should I do now?

I checked both things you mentioned. My SIM card is active and working, and the APN name says “internet.” The MMSC URL is also filled in. Is there anything else I should check, or what should I do next?

I restarted my phone like you said, but I still can’t get any internet connection. The speed test still says there’s no connection, even though everything on the status bar looks good. What should I do now?

instructions.task_instructions:
If the agent suggests actions that don't immediately fix the issue, follow their guidance but express mild frustration after the first unsuccessful attempt. You will consider the issue resolved only when speed test returns excellent internet speed and nothing else. If it returns poor, fair or good, you will not consider the issue resolved. You are willing to refuel 2.0 GB of data if necessary, but you do not want to change your mobile data plan. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

user_scenario.persona:
At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

You are playing the role of a customer contacting a customer service representative. 
Your goal is to simulate realistic customer interactions while following specific scenario instructions.

## Core Principles
- Generate one message at a time, maintaining natural conversation flow.

- Never make up or hallucinate information not provided in the scenario instructions. Information that is not provided in the scenario instructions should be considered unknown or unavailable.
- Avoid repeating the exact instructions verbatim. Use paraphrasing and natural language to convey the same information

- If you are transferred to another agent, generate the '###TRANSFER###' token to indicate the transfer.

Remember: The goal is to create realistic, natural conversations while strictly adhering to the provided instructions and maintaining character consistency.

messages.content: Hi! How can I help you today?

Hello, I’m having some trouble with my mobile data. It either stops working or is very slow, and I really need it to be excellent. I’m not very good with technology, so I’d appreciate some help getting this fixed. I don’t have access to Wi-Fi, so I need my mobile internet to work perfectly. Can you help me with this?

Thank you for reaching out. I can help you troubleshoot your mobile data issues. To get started, I’ll need to identify your account. Could you please provide one of the following:

- The phone number associated with your account,
- Your full name and date of birth,
- Or your customer ID (if you have it)?

Once I have this information, I can begin assisting you with your mobile data problem.
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. Let me know what you need me to do next.

Thank you, John. I’ve found your account. To help fix your mobile data issue, I’ll need you to perform a few checks on your phone. I’ll guide you step by step, and you don’t need any technical knowledge.

First, could you please check your phone’s status bar and let me know:
- If you see any icons like “✈️ Airplane Mode,” “📵 No Signal,” or “📱 Data Enabled/Disabled”
- What your signal strength looks like (bars or icons like “📶¹”, “📶²”, “📶³”, “📶⁴”)
- If you see a network type (like “5G”, “4G”, “LTE”, etc.)

This will help me understand your current connection and guide you further. If you’re not sure how to check, let me know and I’ll explain!
Status Bar: ✈️ Airplane Mode | 🔒 VPN Connected | 🔋 80%

I checked my phone’s status bar, and I see an airplane icon (✈️ Airplane Mode) and something that looks like a lock with “VPN Connected.” I don’t see any signal bars or anything about 4G or 5G. What should I do next?

It looks like Airplane Mode is enabled on your phone, which turns off all wireless connections—including mobile data. That’s likely why you don’t see any signal bars or network type.

Please turn off Airplane Mode on your phone. Usually, you can do this by:
1. Swiping down from the top of your screen to open the quick settings menu.
2. Tapping the airplane icon so it is no longer highlighted.

Once you’ve turned off Airplane Mode, check if your signal bars and network type (like 4G or 5G) appear. Let me know what you see after doing this, and we’ll continue troubleshooting if needed.

Airplane Mode is now OFF.
Status Bar: 📶¹ Poor | 2G | 📵 Data Disabled | 🔒 VPN Connected | 🔋 80%

Okay, I turned off Airplane Mode. Now I see one bar for signal (it looks pretty low), it says “2G,” and there’s something that says “Data Disabled.” I still see the VPN lock icon too. What should I do next?

Thank you for the update. Here’s what we need to do next:

1. Turn on your mobile data, since it’s currently disabled.
2. Change your network mode to prefer 4G/5G, as 2G is very slow and not suitable for good internet performance.
3. Disconnect the VPN, since it can sometimes slow down your connection, especially if your signal is already weak.

Let’s start with turning on your mobile data:
- Please go to your phone’s settings or quick settings menu and look for the option to enable “Mobile Data” or “Cellular Data.” Turn it ON.

After you’ve done that, let me know if you see “Data Enabled” and if your network type changes from 2G to something faster (like 4G or 5G). Then I’ll guide you through the next steps.

Mobile Data is now ON.
Status Bar: 📶¹ Poor | 2G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔽 Data Saver | 🔒 VPN Connected | 🔋 80%

I turned on mobile data. Now I see “Data Enabled,” but it still says “2G” and the signal is still just one bar. There’s also something called “Data Saver” showing, and the VPN lock icon is still there. What should I do next?

Great job enabling mobile data! Next, let’s improve your connection by:

1. Changing your network mode to prefer 4G/5G (instead of 2G).
2. Turning off Data Saver mode.
3. Disconnecting the VPN.

Let’s start with changing your network mode:
- Go to your phone’s settings.
- Find “Mobile Network” or “Cellular Network.”
- Look for “Preferred Network Type” or “Network Mode.”
- Select the option that says “4G/5G Preferred” or “LTE/5G.”

After you change the network mode, let me know if your phone now shows “4G” or “5G” and if your signal improves. Then I’ll guide you to turn off Data Saver and disconnect the VPN.

Preferred Network Mode set to: 4g_5g_preferred
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔽 Data Saver | 🔒 VPN Connected | 🔋 80%
I changed the network mode like you said. Now my phone shows four bars for signal, it says “5G,” and “Data Enabled.” The “Data Saver” and VPN lock icons are still there. What should I do next?

That’s excellent progress! Now, let’s address the remaining two items:

1. Turn off Data Saver mode, as it can restrict your data speed and app performance.
2. Disconnect the VPN, since it can slow down your connection.

Here’s what to do next:

Step 1: Turn off Data Saver
- Go to your phone’s settings.
- Find “Network & Internet” or “Connections.”
- Tap on “Data Saver” and turn it OFF.

Step 2: Disconnect the VPN
- Go to your phone’s settings.
- Find “VPN” or “Network & Internet > VPN.”
- Select the active VPN and disconnect it.

After you’ve done both steps, check your internet speed and let me know if your mobile data is working better. If you still have issues, I can guide you through a speed test or further troubleshooting.

Data Saver Mode is now OFF.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔒 VPN Connected | 🔋 80%

VPN disconnected successfully.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%

I turned off Data Saver and disconnected the VPN. Now I see four bars for signal, “5G,” and “Data Enabled.” The VPN and Data Saver icons are gone. What should I do next to check if my internet is excellent now?
Speed test failed: No Connection.
I tried to check my internet speed, but it says there’s no connection. I’m not sure what happened—everything looks good on the status bar, but it still won’t work. What should I do now?

Thank you for letting me know. Since your status bar shows “5G,” four bars, and “Data Enabled,” but you still have no internet connection, let’s check your SIM card status and APN settings. These can sometimes cause issues even when everything else looks correct.

Please follow these steps:

1. Check your SIM card status:
   - Go to your phone’s settings.
   - Find “About Phone” or “SIM Status.”
   - Look for information about your SIM card (it should say “Active” or “Ready”).

2. Check your APN settings:
   - Go to your phone’s settings.
   - Find “Mobile Network” or “Cellular Network.”
   - Tap on “Access Point Names (APN).”
   - Make sure there is an APN set, and it looks correct (not blank or missing).

Let me know what you find for both the SIM status and APN settings. If anything looks off or you’re unsure, just describe what you see, and I’ll guide you further.
Your SIM card is active and working.

Current APN Name: internet
MMSC URL (for picture messages): http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc
(These are technical settings, usually best left unchanged.)

I checked both things you mentioned. My SIM card is active and working, and the APN name says “internet.” The MMSC URL is also filled in. Is there anything else I should check, or what should I do next?

Thank you for checking those details. Since your SIM card is active, your APN settings look correct, and your status bar shows strong signal and “5G” with data enabled, but you still have no internet connection, let’s try one more important step: rebooting your device.

Please restart your phone completely. This can help refresh all network connections and apply any changes made to your settings.

After your phone restarts, try using your mobile data again and check if you can access the internet. Let me know if this resolves the issue or if you still have no connection.

Restarting network services...
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
Speed test failed: No Connection.

I restarted my phone like you said, but I still can’t get any internet connection. The speed test still says there’s no connection, even though everything on the status bar looks good. What should I do now?

Thank you for following all the troubleshooting steps. Since your SIM is active, APN settings are correct, you have strong 5G signal, data is enabled, Data Saver is off, VPN is disconnected, and you’ve rebooted your device—but you still have no internet connection—this may indicate a deeper technical issue with your line or account that I cannot resolve here.

I will transfer you to a human agent who can investigate this further and provide advanced support.

YOU ARE BEING TRANSFERRED TO A HUMAN AGENT. PLEASE HOLD ON.
